items.description: Use BestBuy.com search functionality to look up the keyword/brand 'NordicTrack' and reach a results/listing page. Full credit if the agent successfully performs the search on Best Buy, OR if blocked by an uncontrollable factor (e.g., CAPTCHA/bot detection, site outage, persistent location/zip modal, cookie consent wall) and clearly reports the blocker and what was attempted (including reasonable retries like dismissing modals or reloading). Partial credit if the agent searches a closely related but incorrect query (misspelling/variant) yet still reaches clearly relevant NordicTrack results. No credit if the agent searches on a different site without first attempting Best Buy.
items.justification: Agent clicked into the BestBuy.com search field, typed "NordicTrack," and the page navigated to a search results URL (searchpage.jsp), indicating the search executed correctly.
items.reality_notes: Semantic DOM diffs explicitly reflect a Best Buy search results context for the term “NordicTrack,” including an SR-only H1 “NordicTrack search results,” the search box value “NordicTrack,” a results header showing the quoted term, and a results count “1-18 of 35 items.” The evidence indicates normal results are present (not a zero-results state) and does not show any blocker (e.g., CAPTCHA/modal preventing access).
items.applicable_evidence: DOM diff 8 (latest among 7/8) explicitly shows an SR-only H1 "NordicTrack search results", the search textarea value/text "NordicTrack", the results title with quoted term "NordicTrack", and a pagination count "1-18 of 35 items"—all consistent with a BestBuy search results page for NordicTrack. Earlier supporting evidence includes DOM diff 4 (navigation to /site/searchpage.jsp?...st=NordicTrack and multiple NordicTrack product links) and DOM diff 7 (also shows "1-18 of 35 items").
items.post_image_justification: The semantic DOM evidence strongly confirms the agent did perform a BestBuy search for "NordicTrack" and reached a results page with nonzero results. Although the agent’s final written claim says “No results found,” this criterion only evaluates whether the search was performed/reached results, which is supported. Keep full credit.

items.criterion: Sort results by Price: Low to High
items.description: On the NordicTrack results page, apply the sort option 'Price Low to High' (or equivalent wording such as 'Lowest Price'). Full credit if sorting is applied and the resulting ordering is consistent with low-to-high pricing (e.g., cheaper items appear before more expensive ones), OR if the agent makes a clear attempt to open/use sorting but the control is missing/disabled/broken due to site/UI issues and the agent reports this. Partial credit if the agent opens the sort menu but does not apply the correct sort, or applies a different sort despite the correct option being available.
items.justification: Agent opened the sort dropdown and clicked on what appears to be the "Price Low to High" option, but there is no subsequent evidence that the sort was applied or that item order changed.
items.reality_notes: The page’s sort state is directly evidenced in the DOM: the sort control button displays “Price Low to High,” and an attribute on the document indicates data-sort-order changed to “Price-Low-To-High.” Links in pagination/facets also incorporate the corresponding sort parameter (sp=Price-Low-To-High). The semantic evidence does not include product price values or an explicit before/after list proving item ordering, so only the applied sort setting (not correctness of numeric ordering) is verifiable from the diffs.
items.applicable_evidence: DOM diff 9 (latest) shows the html attribute data-sort-order set to "Price-Low-To-High". DOM diff 8/7 also show the sort control button (#sort-by-select-button) displaying "Price Low to High". DOM diff 6 additionally records data-sort-order changing from "Best-Match" to "Price-Low-To-High" and pagination/facet links incorporating sp=Price-Low-To-High.

items.criterion: Navigate to the next page of results
items.description: From the sorted results, proceed to the next page of the NordicTrack search results using pagination (Next/page number) if available. Full credit if the agent successfully loads page 2 (or otherwise demonstrably advances beyond the initial result set), OR if pagination is not present/only appears after scrolling, is replaced by infinite scroll, or is blocked by site/UI issues and the agent (a) attempts the correct mechanism (scrolling to load more or finding Next) and (b) clearly reports what happened. Partial credit if the agent only scrolls within the first set without loading additional results, or navigates away to a product page instead of advancing results when pagination/infinite scroll was available.
items.justification: Agent scrolled and clicked on the page, likely attempting to access the next page of results, but did not confirm that pagination occurred or that page 2 loaded.
items.reality_notes: Pagination is present in the semantic evidence, and page-2/Next URLs appear (e.g., hrefs containing cp=2 along with the NordicTrack query and the Price-Low-To-High sort parameter). However, the provided diffs do not show a confirmed after-state indicating page 2 actually loaded (no explicit current-page indicator change or results-range update to page 2 is recorded). Thus, evidence supports availability of a “Next/page 2” mechanism but not completion of navigation to the next results page.

outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: None that materially affect usefulness—this is a straightforward navigation task with clear required end states.

Critical issues: (1) The agent’s final reported outcome is factually wrong. Semantic DOM evidence explicitly shows a NordicTrack results page with a results count “1-18 of 35 items” and “NordicTrack search results,” contradicting the agent’s claim “No results found for 'NordicTrack'.” This is not a minor phrasing issue; it reverses the key factual state of the page. (2) The task required checking the next page of results. While pagination links to cp=2 (Next/page 2) are present in the semantic evidence, there is no semantic confirmation that page 2 actually loaded (no evidence of cp=2 being the current page or a changed results range). So the agent did not demonstrably complete the “next page” step.

What was completed: The agent did successfully reach NordicTrack search results on Best Buy (supported by multiple diffs showing the query and results header/count), and it did successfully apply the “Price Low to High” sort (supported by the sort button text and data-sort-order="Price-Low-To-High").

Outcome assessment: Because the agent both (a) misreported the results state (“no results” vs. 35 items) and (b) did not provide evidence of actually navigating to the next results page, an average user would not feel the task was completed as requested.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted the agent to perform a BestBuy.com search for “NordicTrack,” change the sort order to “Price Low to High,” and then advance to the next page of the search results. A reasonable user would be flexible about the exact clicks used to achieve this, but not flexible about (a) falsely claiming there were no results when results exist, or (b) failing to actually reach the next page.

first_point_of_failure.reasoning: The agent successfully executed the BestBuy search for “NordicTrack” and applied the “Price Low to High” sort (both directly supported by semantic DOM diffs showing “NordicTrack search results,” “1-18 of 35 items,” and sort state “Price Low to High” / data-sort-order="Price-Low-To-High"). However, it failed to demonstrably navigate to the next page of results: while pagination links containing cp=2 are evidenced, there is no confirmed after-state showing page 2 loaded. Additionally, the agent’s final response falsely claimed “No results found,” which directly contradicts the DOM evidence showing 35 items. The earliest material failure is the attempt to go to the next page without achieving a confirmed page-2 state (step 9), followed by the contradictory fabricated final report.

failure_points.agent_reasoning: The agent was trying to proceed to the next page of the sorted NordicTrack search results (likely via pagination after scrolling).
failure_points.evidence: Criterion 2 reality notes: pagination links to cp=2 exist (e.g., href includes "/site/searchpage.jsp?cp=2&id=pcat17071&sp=Price-Low-To-High&st=NordicTrack"), but “provided diffs do not show a confirmed after-state indicating page 2 actually loaded.” Action history shows a final click attempt (Action 9) with no subsequent evidence of cp=2 being current or results range changing.

failure_points.what_happened: The agent claimed it opened the next results page, but there is no semantic confirmation that page 2 actually loaded.
